concerns.text: The covariate `baseline_sentiment` is derived from the user's OWN comments and is entered as a predictor in Model 1 (Phase 3 Task 15). This directly violates FR-018/Constitution VI ('preventing any feature derived from the user's own comments from being used as a predictor') and creates partial circularity with `self_eval_score` (both are VADER sentiment of the same user's comments — baseline_sentiment is essentially a component of the outcome). Either drop it or derive a genuinely separate baseline (e.g., pre-window sentiment from a distinct time period).

`exposure_level` is defined as a community-level proportion (subreddit aggregate activity), yet the regression is fit at the user level with plain OLS. A subreddit-level predictor applied to user-level outcomes (a) has no within-subreddit variation, (b) requires clustered/robust standard errors or a multilevel model, and (c) 'target subreddits' are never operationally defined — no selection criterion exists anywhere in the plan. Specify the subreddit-selection rule and the dependence structure (clustered SEs by subreddit or mixed model).

Identifying 'the content a user is exposed to' requires knowing which subreddits the user visits — operationally, the user's own comment locations. So all three 'exposure-stream' predictors are conditioned on the user's own behavior, partially conflating predictor and outcome streams despite the claimed Principle VI separation. The plan should acknowledge this exposure-identification circularity as a limitation and state precisely how exposure content is assigned to a user (e.g., subreddits posted in vs. subscribed vs. all of Reddit).

FR-017 requires demographic proxies from user PROFILE METADATA ('about' fields); Task 9 derives them from user TEXT. Pushshift comment dumps typically lack profile metadata — either state the data field used or acknowledge the deviation from the spec's stated source.
